t.5.63.1: Then, having gone to Mount Prasravaṇa and its wondrous forest, they bowed their heads to Rāma and to the mighty Lakṣmaṇa.
t.5.63.2: Placing the crown prince at their head and saluting Sugrīva, they then began to relate the news of Sītā.
t.5.63.3: Her confinement in Rāvaṇa's inner apartments, the threats from the rākṣasīs, her deep devotion to Rāma, and also the time limit that had been set.
t.5.63.4: All those monkeys reported this in the presence of Rāma; and Rāma, having heard that Vaidehī was unharmed, spoke these words in reply.
t.5.63.5: Where does the divine Sītā dwell, and how does she feel toward me? O monkeys, tell me all this concerning Vaidehī.
t.5.63.6: Having heard the words of Rāma, the monkeys, in Rāma's presence, urged on Hanūmān, who knew all the news of Sītā.
t.5.63.7: Having heard their words, Hanūmān, the son of Māruta, skilled in speech, spoke and told how he had seen Sītā.
t.5.63.8: Having leapt across the ocean, a hundred yojanas in extent, I went on, searching for Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, in my longing to see her.
t.5.63.9: There, on the southern shore of the southern ocean, lies the city called Laṅkā, belonging to the evil-minded Rāvaṇa.
t.5.63.10: There, in Rāvaṇa's inner apartments, I saw Sītā, O Rāma. The lovely lady stays alive only because she has set all her heart's desire on you.
t.5.63.11: She was seen by me in the midst of rākṣasīs, threatened again and again, guarded in the pleasure-grove by hideous rākṣasīs.
t.5.63.12: Your queen, though she was never accustomed to sorrow, is suffering sorrow, confined in Rāvaṇa's inner palace and closely guarded by rākṣasīs.
t.5.63.13: Wearing her hair in a single braid, wretched, wholly absorbed in thoughts of you, sleeping on the bare ground, her limbs pale, she is like a lotus pond at the coming of winter.
t.5.63.14: O Kākutstha, the queen, who had turned away from Rāvaṇa and resolved to die, her mind fixed on you, was somehow found by me after a long search.
t.5.63.16: Then the queen was addressed and shown the whole matter; and having heard of the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva, she was filled with joy.
t.5.63.15: O sinless one, by softly proclaiming the renown of the Ikṣvāku lineage, I brought her to trust, O tiger among men.
t.5.63.17: Her conduct is disciplined, and so too is her devotion to you; thus did I see the illustrious daughter of Janaka, O bull among men, given to fierce austerity through her devotion to you.
t.5.63.18: And she gave me a token of recognition, O greatly wise Rāghava: the account of what happened concerning the crow in your presence at Citrakūṭa.
t.5.63.19: "And Rāma, tiger among men, must be informed by you, O son of Vāyu, in full of all that you have seen here": thus Jānakī spoke to me.
t.5.63.20: And this, carefully and well guarded, is to be handed over to him by you, speaking these words thus while Sugrīva listens.
t.5.63.21: "This splendid crest-jewel has been carefully guarded by me for you; and remember the tilaka mark of red arsenic," so she said.
t.5.63.22: This splendid water-born jewel has been sent back to you by me. Beholding it, I shall rejoice in my misfortune as though I were beholding you, O sinless one.
t.5.63.23: I shall sustain my life for one month, O son of Daśaratha; beyond a month I could not live, fallen as I am into the power of the rākṣasas.
t.5.63.24: Thus spoke Sītā to me, she of emaciated limbs, devoted to dharma, confined in Rāvaṇa's inner palace, her eyes wide open like a doe's.
t.5.63.25: All this, O Rāghava, I have told you exactly as it happened. By every means, let a crossing over the waters of the ocean be arranged.
t.5.63.26: Knowing that the two princes had regained their confidence, and having handed that token of recognition to Rāghava, the son of Vāyu related in full, in his own words and in due order, everything that the queen had told him.
